claims.text: Machine-learning-driven optimization of SPS parameters will enable a narrowly defined transient-liquid-phase regime.
The transient-liquid-phase regime will promote complete in situ wetting of W surfaces by Cu.
Complete in situ Cu wetting of W will minimize void formation.
Complete in situ Cu wetting of W will suppress phase separation.
A uniform, defect-minimized W–Cu interfacial structure will improve thermal transport.
A uniform, defect-minimized W–Cu interfacial structure will maintain mechanical durability under irradiation.
Conventional SPS or transient-liquid-phase sintering of W–Cu has previously produced residual voids, defects, and undesirable phase separation.
Relative to conventional SPS, ML-optimized SPS will produce significantly fewer interfacial voids and defects.
Relative to conventional SPS, ML-optimized SPS will improve W–Cu interfacial integrity.
Relative to conventional SPS, ML-optimized SPS will enhance the thermal conductivity of the W–Cu composite.
Relative to conventional SPS, ML-optimized SPS will provide robust mechanical durability under fusion-relevant irradiation.
The process must remain below Cu's boiling point while entering the transient-liquid-phase regime.
Scalability of the optimized SPS parameters is uncertain.
Long-term performance under actual irradiation conditions is uncertain.
Minor voids may persist if the transient liquid phase is not fully controlled.
